question.text: 'Kaveri Infra Debt AIF' is being set up as an ONSHORE Indian AIF that will attract BOTH domestic and FPI commitments into a single onshore pool. Under which regulatory route does an FPI contribute to such an onshore AIF?

answer.text: FDI Automatic Route; no Ministry of Finance or RBI approval required
Government Approval Route; MOF approval mandatory

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.5.2: in a Unified / onshore structure that accepts FPI commitments, FDI Policy's automatic route applies — no MOF or RBI approval is required. This is a significant ease-of-structuring point. The Trap: Option B unnecessarily complicates. Option C applies only to pure offshore pooling by FVCI-registered funds. Option D is for resident Indian outbound remittance, not inbound FPI. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B touch FPI route superficially. XIX-C tests the automatic-route nuance for FPI-into-onshore-AIF flows. Manager's Pro-Tip: Document FPI KYC and FATCA/CRS carefully — automatic route entry does not mean automatic compliance. Your Fund Administrator should run periodic FATCA refresh every 3 years.
